title: Gerbrandy Tower
visualBrief: Current hybrid broadcast tower: 100 m concrete shaft, two glazed balcony rings, six open equipment galleries, 2 m steel pipe mast, reportage cabin, individual antenna arrays and twelve guys to the three mapped anchor blocks.

nativeAxes.front: +X east, +Z south; the three unequal mapped guy-anchor vectors determine site orientation
nativeAxes.origin: Center of the exact-QID concrete shaft footprint, Y=0 at local terrain contact

scaleBasis: Current owner Cellnex and fire-system installer Saval give 372 m total, approximately 100 m concrete and a 2 m diameter steel tube. RCE confirms the concrete shaft and two glazed balconies. Contemporary contractor photographs determine balcony rhythm, cabin, arrays and intermediate guy bands. Exact-QID OSM shaft and surveyed connected anchor-block footprints supply independent horizontal geometry.

geographicProposal.evidence: Native +X east, +Z south. Round shaft has no principal horizontal axis; mapped asymmetric guy-anchor positions provide actual orientation.
geographicProposal.limitations: Anchor is the exact-QID circular shaft center. The three guy blocks use their actual surveyed footprint positions, not a symmetric invented triangle. Guy attachment heights other than the published 226 m level are reconstructed from current contractor photographs; all local geometry shares the concrete shaft terrain-contact datum. Surrounding polder is nearly flat; detailed foundation grading remains approximate.

limitations: Retained372m envelope,100m shaft,2m pipe and mapped three-anchor topology govern the model. Alternate374/367m figures remain recorded in the detailed source. Balcony/equipment elevations, window phase and guy bands at122/302/350m remain photographic reconstruction;226m band and approximately220m cabin use retained published controls.

All three foundations share the shaft terrain datum. Native polder grading/anchor contact has not been newly verified. Independent equipment buildings, below-ground works and seasonal Christmas strings remain outside this permanent tower asset.

Detailed source equipment and dimensions are retained; inverted foundation winding and concrete/glazing clipping are corrected. Skyline aggregates window coverage and thin antenna/rail details; district uses sparse guards, seven aggregate racks and two-sided thin mast platforms. Street/closeup restore finer details; cable paths keep all12 connections with illustrative sag. No physical-device timing or engineering tension/collision certification.
reviewStatus: medium-fi; current hash-bound visual acceptance recorded in qa.json

appearance.identity: 372m hybrid broadcast tower with100m concrete shaft, lower and upper glazed balconies plus narrow top glazing, six open equipment galleries, nine radomes,2m pipe mast, octagonal reportage cabin, antenna banks and twelve guy cables reaching all three unequal mapped foundations.
appearance.master: Retain the full detailed master and original equipment. Normalize one inverted mapped foundation ring, and refine the narrow top glazing facets so they stay outside the concrete core. Heights, radii and equipment stations are retained.
appearance.browser: Four complete source-local levels retain the whole tower and guy-anchor layout. Skyline has996triangles, all twelve continuously joined cables, three foundations, all gallery/platform stations, glazed rings, cabin and digital tip; tiny windows, rails and antenna racks aggregate. District retains all92 window positions, seven aggregate racks per side and coarse thin mast platforms; street restores full14-rack banks, curved guards and window openings. Closeup restores detailed fittings, real window-frame reveals, bolt-head faces and fine connected cable paths. Shared concrete and painted-metal graphs are reused without images.
